toyota_summary:
Britain told the EU today it won't sign a binding agreement to raise tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, breaking ranks with Brussels over how to handle Beijing's market dominance. The move signals a willingness to let Chinese imports flow into the UK at lower cost than on the continent, undercutting EU automakers on price.

This matters because it could fracture the West's coordinated response to Chinese competition. If Britain becomes a cheaper entry point for Chinese EVs into European supply chains, it pressures other countries to either match lower tariffs or watch their market share erode. It also gives Chinese battery and vehicle makers a legal arbitrage play they didn't have before.

Watch whether other non-EU countries follow Britain's lead within the next two weeks.

---

Yemen's government warned shipping companies today to stop paying protection fees to Houthi militias controlling the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandeb strait, the critical chokepoint through which roughly one-fifth of global container traffic passes. The warning has no enforcement mechanism and the militias have continued seizures despite it.

For automakers, this means continued supply chain unpredictability. Transit times through Suez remain 50 percent longer than pre-2023 levels because ships still divert around Africa, raising logistics costs and delivery times for parts and finished vehicles. The chaotic situation—where neither Yemen's government nor international navies have restored normal passage—keeps the risk premium in place indefinitely.

The real tell will be whether insurance premiums stabilize or spike again if Houthi attacks accelerate.

emails.subject: How to get robotaxis on Europe’s streets
emails.subject_en: How to get robotaxis on Europe’s streets
emails.summary_en: Industry experts say Europe's robotaxi ambitions are being held back by fragmented national permitting rules, even as pilot projects multiply across cities like Zagreb. Uber and other backers argue autonomous vehicles could dramatically cut traffic deaths and improve mobility access, but warn that bureaucratic delays—sometimes six months just for a testing permit—are slowing the shift from trials to commercial scale. The message from Monday's conference: without unified EU-wide rules, Europe risks falling behind in the robotaxi race.
emails.summary_ja: 欧州では自動運転タクシーの試験プロジェクトが各都市で増加しているが、許認可制度が国ごとに異なるため商用化への移行が妨げられていると専門家は指摘する。Uberなどは、自動運転車が交通事故死を大幅に減らし移動手段の利便性を高める可能性があると主張する一方、試験許可の取得だけで6カ月かかるなど官僚的な遅れが課題だと警告した。月曜日に開かれた会議では、EU全体で統一されたルールがなければ欧州はロボタクシー競争で遅れを取りかねないとの見方が示された。

emails.subject: Five common questions about US-Canada relations after the midterms
emails.subject_en: Five common questions about US-Canada relations after the midterms
emails.summary_en: Eurasia Group sees only a 40% chance of a limited US-Canada trade deal by year-end, with talks likely dragging into 2027 as Prime Minister Mark Carney weighs political costs of accepting US tariffs on autos and other goods under USMCA. Despite Democrats' midterm gains, the White House retains control over tariff policy, meaning no quick relief is expected for the auto sector from Section 232 duties. Canadian public skepticism and divisions among officials over accepting any deal involving continued auto tariffs further complicate near-term resolution.
emails.summary_ja: ユーラシア・グループは、年内の米加限定貿易合意の可能性を40%とみており、カーニー首相が自動車などへの対米関税を受け入れる政治的コストを見極める中、交渉は2027年にもつれ込む可能性が高いとしている。民主党の中間選挙での躍進にもかかわらず、関税政策の主導権はホワイトハウスが握り続けており、自動車業界にとって232条関税からの早期救済は期待薄だ。カナダ国内の懐疑的な世論と、自動車関税継続を含む合意受け入れを巡る当局者間の意見対立が、早期解決をさらに難しくしている。
